text:
The evidence can't tell us whether clearing is happening today. It covers only 2021, and the latest year observed in the data is 2025.

For 2021, Hansen mapped about 81.3 ha of tree-cover loss (2.23% of the 3,643.5 ha property). This is well supported: the JRC 2020 forest map agrees on 98% of the affected area. Most of that area (68.1 ha) is mapped as planted pine (Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda). None is native forest, and 13.2 ha is outside mapped forest. A further 37.3 ha was lost in patches under 0.5 ha, which are not counted as an event.

This loss is not evidence of deforestation. Hansen counts any stand replacement, including harvesting a plantation. The data also doesn't show the cause, whether the change was legal, who was responsible, or any compliance status.

To answer your question, you would need loss data for 2022 onward and more recent imagery.
